    def test_service_catalog_is_not_hardcoded_in_react():
        """React receives the catalog through the view-model; it owns no copy.
    
        Checked on the component source with comments stripped (prose may name the
        constant it must NOT copy): no service name, group label or code literal may
        appear in the shipped TypeScript. The only legal path for that data is the
        ``financeServiceCatalog`` slice delivered by the backend.
        """
        import re as _re
    
        from core.config import GETFLY_SERVICES_LIST
    
        sources = [
            path for path in COMPONENT_SRC.rglob("*")
            if path.suffix in {".ts", ".tsx"} and path.is_file()
        ]
        assert sources, "the component source tree must be inspectable"
        raw = "\n".join(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for path in sources)
        # Strip block and line comments so a documented reference to the canonical
        # source is not mistaken for a copied list.
        code = _re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", raw, flags=_re.S)
        code = "\n".join(line.split("//", 1)[0] for line in code.splitlines())
    
        # A copied catalog would show up as service-name and group-label string
        # literals (codes like "EXW" double as Incoterms, so they prove nothing).
        literals = set(_re.findall(r'"([^"\n]+)"', code)) | set(_re.findall(r"'([^'\n]+)'", code))
        for item in GETFLY_SERVICES_LIST:
            for field in ("name", "group"):
                value = str(item.get(field) or "").strip()
>               assert value not in literals, f"catalog {field} '{value}' is hard-coded in React"

    def _assert_build_read_budget(result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Regression guard for LOGI_INTERACTION_LATENCY_FINALIZE_02.
    
        Inside the ONE post-action build every reference collection is read at
        most ONCE and nothing is read per contract or per shipment.  The two
        ``shipments`` reads are the worklist itself and the bounded id projection
        the finance worklists need (archived shipments included).
    
        Issue #195 — the total bound was recalibrated from 18 to 26: the product
        has grown since PR74 (Admin-published uploaded templates need the
        app_settings registry, the NotebookLM registry, work-module templates),
        and each of those is a bounded once-per-build read, not an N+1.  The
        strict guards that actually catch N+1 regressions stay: no
        contracts.find_one, every collection's find at most once (app_settings at
        most 3: one shared uploaded-template registry read, one effective-catalog
        build, one NotebookLM registry), and nothing per shipment.
        """
        ops = _build_ops_by_collection(result)
        assert ops.get("contracts.find_one", 0) == 0, ops   # was one read PER CONTRACT
        assert ops.get("app_settings.find_one", 0) <= 3, ops  # shared reads, never per shipment
        for collection in ("customers", "contracts", "quotes", "tasks", "agreements",
                           "authority_companies", "authority_agents", "docgen_documents",
                           "shipment_attachments", "audit_logs", "knowledge_base", "users",
                           "financial_obligations", "financial_transactions", "financial_allocations"):
            assert ops.get(f"{collection}.find", 0) <= 1, (collection, ops)
        assert ops.get("shipments.find", 0) <= 2, ops

    def _assert_build_read_budget(result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Regression guard for LOGI_INTERACTION_LATENCY_FINALIZE_02.
    
        Inside the ONE post-action build every reference collection is read at
        most ONCE and nothing is read per contract or per shipment.  The two
        ``shipments`` reads are the worklist itself and the bounded id projection
        the finance worklists need (archived shipments included).
    
        Issue #195 — the total bound was recalibrated from 18 to 26: the product
        has grown since PR74 (Admin-published uploaded templates need the
        app_settings registry, the NotebookLM registry, work-module templates),
        and each of those is a bounded once-per-build read, not an N+1.  The
        strict guards that actually catch N+1 regressions stay: no
        contracts.find_one, every collection's find at most once (app_settings at
        most 3: one shared uploaded-template registry read, one effective-catalog
        build, one NotebookLM registry), and nothing per shipment.
        """
        ops = _build_ops_by_collection(result)
        assert ops.get("contracts.find_one", 0) == 0, ops   # was one read PER CONTRACT
        assert ops.get("app_settings.find_one", 0) <= 3, ops  # shared reads, never per shipment
        for collection in ("customers", "contracts", "quotes", "tasks", "agreements",
                           "authority_companies", "authority_agents", "docgen_documents",
                           "shipment_attachments", "audit_logs", "knowledge_base", "users",
                           "financial_obligations", "financial_transactions", "financial_allocations"):
            assert ops.get(f"{collection}.find", 0) <= 1, (collection, ops)
        assert ops.get("shipments.find", 0) <= 2, ops

    def _assert_build_read_budget(result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Regression guard for LOGI_INTERACTION_LATENCY_FINALIZE_02.
    
        Inside the ONE post-action build every reference collection is read at
        most ONCE and nothing is read per contract or per shipment.  The two
        ``shipments`` reads are the worklist itself and the bounded id projection
        the finance worklists need (archived shipments included).
    
        Issue #195 — the total bound was recalibrated from 18 to 26: the product
        has grown since PR74 (Admin-published uploaded templates need the
        app_settings registry, the NotebookLM registry, work-module templates),
        and each of those is a bounded once-per-build read, not an N+1.  The
        strict guards that actually catch N+1 regressions stay: no
        contracts.find_one, every collection's find at most once (app_settings at
        most 3: one shared uploaded-template registry read, one effective-catalog
        build, one NotebookLM registry), and nothing per shipment.
        """
        ops = _build_ops_by_collection(result)
        assert ops.get("contracts.find_one", 0) == 0, ops   # was one read PER CONTRACT
        assert ops.get("app_settings.find_one", 0) <= 3, ops  # shared reads, never per shipment
        for collection in ("customers", "contracts", "quotes", "tasks", "agreements",
                           "authority_companies", "authority_agents", "docgen_documents",
                           "shipment_attachments", "audit_logs", "knowledge_base", "users",
                           "financial_obligations", "financial_transactions", "financial_allocations"):
            assert ops.get(f"{collection}.find", 0) <= 1, (collection, ops)
        assert ops.get("shipments.find", 0) <= 2, ops

    def _assert_build_read_budget(result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Regression guard for LOGI_INTERACTION_LATENCY_FINALIZE_02.
    
        Inside the ONE post-action build every reference collection is read at
        most ONCE and nothing is read per contract or per shipment.  The two
        ``shipments`` reads are the worklist itself and the bounded id projection
        the finance worklists need (archived shipments included).
    
        Issue #195 — the total bound was recalibrated from 18 to 26: the product
        has grown since PR74 (Admin-published uploaded templates need the
        app_settings registry, the NotebookLM registry, work-module templates),
        and each of those is a bounded once-per-build read, not an N+1.  The
        strict guards that actually catch N+1 regressions stay: no
        contracts.find_one, every collection's find at most once (app_settings at
        most 3: one shared uploaded-template registry read, one effective-catalog
        build, one NotebookLM registry), and nothing per shipment.
        """
        ops = _build_ops_by_collection(result)
        assert ops.get("contracts.find_one", 0) == 0, ops   # was one read PER CONTRACT
        assert ops.get("app_settings.find_one", 0) <= 3, ops  # shared reads, never per shipment
        for collection in ("customers", "contracts", "quotes", "tasks", "agreements",
                           "authority_companies", "authority_agents", "docgen_documents",
                           "shipment_attachments", "audit_logs", "knowledge_base", "users",
                           "financial_obligations", "financial_transactions", "financial_allocations"):
            assert ops.get(f"{collection}.find", 0) <= 1, (collection, ops)
        assert ops.get("shipments.find", 0) <= 2, ops

    def test_adversarial_reverting_to_baseline_produces_double_build_and_rerun(self) -> None:
        """Adversarial check: if callback does NOT run before script body (old baseline),
        the system does two full VM builds and triggers an explicit st.rerun."""
        trigger = {
            "shipment_field_save": {
                "seq": 1,
                "event": "shipment_field_save",
                "payload": {"shipmentId": "LO-0306", "fields": {"booking_no": "BK-ADV-01"}},
            }
        }
        bvm_calls: list[int] = []
        rerun_calls: list[int] = []
        from streamlit.components.v2.bidi_component.state import ComponentResult
    
        run_count = [0]
        def fake_renderer(**kw):
            if run_count[0] == 0:
                return ComponentResult({}, trigger)
            return ComponentResult({}, {})
    
        # Simulate OLD BASELINE: callback is lambda: None (no-op prefix),
        # so dispatch only runs post-render.
        with patch("views.logi_view_model.build_view_model", side_effect=lambda: bvm_calls.append(1) or {"version": 1}), \
             patch("streamlit.rerun", side_effect=lambda: rerun_calls.append(1)), \
             patch("views.logi_shell._renderer", return_value=fake_renderer), \
             patch("views.web_app.require_login", return_value={"username": "test_user", "role": "admin"}), \
             patch("core.database.save_shipment_atomic", return_value=True):
    
            # Old baseline run 1: (no callback, script body runs)
            web_app.main()
            # In old baseline, dispatch called st.rerun
            if rerun_calls:
                run_count[0] += 1
                web_app.main()
    
        # Under baseline: build_view_model was called TWICE, rerun was called ONCE

    def test_pxk_operator_identity_generates_persisted_office_file(staging, event_seq):
        """PXK: operator-supplied legal identity → real generation → persistence.
    
        LOGI_REAL_USE_READINESS_01 repair pin. core.docgen refuses to invent the
        lot's own ``pxk_no`` / ``pxk_date`` (as the authoritative docgen desk does,
        they are operator inputs), so without them the gate must stay fail-closed
        and NAME the missing facts. With them, the real service must produce an
        OOXML file, persist canonical document metadata, and the fresh view model
        must read the document back (number/date/done + downloadable bytes) — the
        UI used to drop all three and only showed a toast.

            "deliveryLocation": "Kho An Phát — KCN Quế Võ"})
